text: What is the Spring Boot annotation to mark the main application class?
explanation:
@SpringBootApplication is correct because it combines @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan, so it is the standard annotation on the main Spring Boot class.

Example: a typical entry point looks like this:

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;

@SpringBootApplication
public class DemoApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args);
    }
}

text: Which dependency is typically used for building REST APIs in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-web is correct because it pulls in the dependencies needed for REST controllers, JSON serialization, and the embedded servlet container used by most Spring Boot APIs.

Example: after adding that starter, you can expose an endpoint like this:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/users")
public class UserController {
    @GetMapping
    public List<String> findAll() {
        return List.of("Alice", "Bob");
    }
}

text: In Spring, which annotation is used for constructor-based dependency injection?
explanation:
@Autowired is correct because Spring uses it to inject a matching bean, and it is commonly seen on constructors when wiring required dependencies.

Example:

@Service
public class OrderService {
    private final PaymentService paymentService;

    @Autowired
    public OrderService(PaymentService paymentService) {
        this.paymentService = paymentService;
    }
}

text: Which file defines Spring profiles and properties for different environments?
explanation:
application.properties is correct because that file is the conventional place to keep Spring Boot configuration such as ports, profiles, logging, and datasource properties.

Example:

server.port=8081
spring.profiles.active=dev
logging.level.org.springframework.web=DEBUG

text: Which Spring module provides integration with relational databases using repositories?
explanation:
Spring Data JPA is correct because it provides repository abstractions and JPA integration so relational data access can be written with much less boilerplate.

Example:

@Entity
public class Customer {
    @Id
    private Long id;
}

public interface CustomerRepository extends JpaRepository<Customer, Long> {
}

text: In Spring Data JPA, which annotation marks the primary key of an entity?
explanation:
@Id is correct because JPA uses @Id to mark the field or property that represents the primary key of an entity.

Example:

@Entity
public class Product {
    @Id
    private Long id;
    private String name;
}

text: What is the default port for a Spring Boot application?
explanation:
8080 is correct because Spring Boot listens on port 8080 by default unless you override server.port.

Example: if you run the app locally with default settings, you usually open http://localhost:8080.

text: Which annotation maps an HTTP GET request to a controller method?
explanation:
@GetMapping is correct because it is the shortcut annotation for mapping HTTP GET requests to a controller method.

Example:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/books")
public class BookController {
    @GetMapping
    public List<String> list() {
        return List.of("Spring in Action");
    }
}

text: Which Spring Boot starter adds actuator endpoints for monitoring?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-actuator is correct because it adds production-ready endpoints for health checks, metrics, and application diagnostics.

Example: after adding the starter, endpoints such as /actuator/health can be exposed for monitoring.

text: Which Spring annotation secures methods or classes?
explanation:
@PreAuthorize is correct because it is a Spring Security annotation used to enforce authorization rules before a method is executed.

Example:

@Service
public class AdminService {
    @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
    public void deleteUser(Long id) {
    }
}

text: Which Spring annotation maps a class to a REST controller?
explanation:
@RestController is correct because it combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, which makes it the standard choice for JSON-based APIs.

Example:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/health")
public class HealthController {
    @GetMapping
    public Map<String, String> health() {
        return Map.of("status", "UP");
    }
}

text: Which Spring component scans for annotated classes during startup?
explanation:
Component scanning is correct because Spring uses component scanning to discover classes annotated with stereotypes such as @Component, @Service, and @Repository.

Example:

@Component
public class AuditFormatter {
}

text: In Spring Boot, which file enables configuring logging levels?
explanation:
application.properties is correct because that file is the conventional place to keep Spring Boot configuration such as ports, profiles, logging, and datasource properties.

Example:

server.port=8081
spring.profiles.active=dev
logging.level.org.springframework.web=DEBUG
